summary.headline: Mold-Tek Q1 FY27 per-kg EBITDA rose to INR46.7 (from ~INR40.7 in FY26) on consolidation and mix, while volume grew only ~6% due to a 17% lube drop.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a record quarter, with turnover crossing INR300 crores and EBITDA per kg at INR46.7 versus INR40.7 for full FY26. The company attributes the margin gain mainly to consolidating Hyderabad units from 5 to 2, lower overheads, wastage and inter-unit transfers, and a higher share of pharma and Food & FMCG. Volume growth was about 6%, held back by a 17% fall in lube volumes linked to base-oil shortages at some clients, while paint grew 10.8% in volume and Food & FMCG and pharma grew 24% and 38%. Revenue growth was inflated by raw-material pass-through (PP copolymer rose from about INR107/kg in Q4 to about INR130/kg in Q1), and working capital and finance cost rose sharply as a result.

segments.name: Paints (decorative)
segments.commentary: Value ~46% of revenue, volume ~50% (management); volume grew 10.8% and value ~31%, with growth from existing clients and rising IML adoption. Management expects paint's share to fall toward ~40% over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Lubes
segments.commentary: Volume fell 17% due to base-oil shortages at some private clients affected by the Iran war; lube EBITDA is about INR35-40/kg. Management expects recovery in the current quarter.

segments.name: Food & FMCG (incl. Qpack)
segments.commentary: Food & FMCG grew 24.2% (26% per analyst); Food is ~24% of sales and ~28-29% including Qpack. Management targets 18-20% CAGR.

segments.name: Qpack
segments.commentary: Growth slowed to ~2% from ~20% in the prior quarter because edible oil and cashew customers were price-sensitive; some customers moved back to tin. Management expects ~10% growth in Q2 and double digits later.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Revenue up 41% (volume up 38%) YoY; FY26 base INR34 crores with FY27 target INR50-55 crores. Pharma is ~3.5% of sales but only ~2% of volume.

segments.name: Vibe (JV)
segments.commentary: Three products have patent applications and further products are at pilot stage; commercial products expected around Q3 FY27, with a couple of crores of revenue possible in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA per kg target raised to INR44-45 (from INR42-43); management says it expects to beat INR42 comfortably.
Volume growth target of 10-12% for FY27; management says ~10% is achievable and paint could grow 10-15%.
FY27 capex cut to ~INR90 crores (from INR130-135 crores), including INR25-30 crores for pharma.
Management expects EBITDA growth of 18-20% with volume growth near 10%, and sees the 19-20% EBITDA growth as sustainable for the rest of the year.
Capacity additions of 10-12% a year; target to lift utilisation from ~75% to 78-80%, plus 8-10% new capacity.
capex_capacity: Total capacity is ~67,000 MTPA across Cheyyar, Panipat and Mahad; management says utilisation is about 75%.
Panipat thin-wall trials on 4 machines sell INR70 lakhs-1 crore a month, doubling from August; Qpack sales from Panipat were INR1-1.5 crores in the last six months.
Ophthalmic range: 25,000 sq ft building under construction at the current facility, due in ~6 months; commercial molds are 5-6 months away. Trial molds are complete.

Medical devices (dosing pens): planned minimum capacity of 1 million pens per month; the new land is reserved for devices, and a plant needs 50,000-60,000 sq ft, INR10 crores building and INR10-15 crores machinery.
Automation and lean-manufacturing study planned with a Chinese partner, with implementation expected in the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Raw-material costs were passed through to clients in the following month; management says the company recovered the full increase while keeping margins.
PP copolymer price peaked near INR155-160/kg in late March/April, was ~INR145-146/kg at the time of the call, and management expects it could fall to INR120-125/kg if the war ends.
Inventory gain in Q1 estimated at INR1-1.5/kg.
Realisation benefit: management said ~INR3/kg came from higher pharma and FMCG realisation and ~INR3/kg from consolidation and efficiencies.
Raw-material availability is better than in March-April, though pricing remains volatile. Company inventory is about 1 month (raw material, SFG and finished goods).
